# Results -- Study 295 (Stablecoin-Supply) on the real BTC tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join the
curated monthly **total stablecoin supply** series ($bn, USDT + USDC + DAI +
BUSD + the long tail) with the BTC-USD monthly tape; build a one-month-lagged
**dry-powder timing signal** (hold BTC next month when supply grew this month,
else flat) and a **predictive regression** of next-month BTC return on
standardised supply growth.  Pinned against buy-and-hold BTC and a
contemporaneous (non-tradable) regression that exposes reflexivity.
**Single-asset BTC spot: price-only == total-return (no dividend).** The supply
series is a curated public aggregate (noted on the Signal axis). As-of
**2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Curated stablecoin supply ($bn, month-end) | 2018-01 -> 2026-05 | 101 months | -- |
| yfinance BTC-USD monthly close (auto-adj) | 2018-01-31 -> 2026-05-31 | 101 months | `41dff5f08708` |
| Joined panel (supply, btc_ret) | 2018-01-31 -> 2026-05-31 | 101 months x 2 | `ae8e27f23d83` |

Execution: signal observed at month-end *t* (supply growth over month *t*), the
position is applied to the BTC return earned in month *t+1* -- **one-month
execution lag**. Switching cost charged one-way on traded NAV.

## Primary specification -- supply-timed (long/flat) vs buy-and-hold BTC

| Series | Mean return | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | Max DD |
|--------|-------------|-------------|---------|--------|
| Buy-and-hold BTC | +41.2%/yr | +0.61 | +1.51 | -73% |
| **Supply-timed (long 77 / flat 24 mo)** | +49.5%/yr | +0.85 | **+2.09** | -50% |
| **Excess (timed - BTC)** | +8.3%/yr | -- | **+0.72** | -- |

- The timed series *looks* better than buy-and-hold (higher Sharpe, shallower
  drawdown) -- but the **excess over buy-and-hold has HAC *t* = +0.72**, i.e.
  the apparent improvement is **not statistically distinguishable from beta
  timing during a single secular BTC bull market**.  The strategy is long BTC in
  77 of 101 months; most of its return is just BTC's drift.
- Block-bootstrap 95% CI on the **excess Sharpe = [-0.42, +0.90]** with **21% of
  resamples negative** -- the CI straddles zero.

## Predictive regression -- the clean forward-information read

`btc_ret(t) ~ a + b * standardised_supply_growth(t - lag)`

| Spec | Slope *b* | HAC *t* | R² | corr | n |
|------|-----------|---------|----|------|---|
| **Lagged (t+1, tradable)** | +0.0417 | **+1.59** | 0.047 | +0.22 | 99 |
| Contemporaneous (t, NOT tradable) | +0.0532 | **+2.15** | 0.077 | +0.28 | 100 |

The **lagged (tradable) slope clears no inference bar: HAC *t* = +1.59 < 2**.
The **contemporaneous slope is larger and significant (t = +2.15)** -- supply
and price move *together*.  Contemporaneous > lagged is the textbook signature
of a **coincident, reflexive series**: supply mints when money is already
flooding in and prices are already rising, which is not tradable.

## Sub-period decay -- the edge is a 2018-2020 artefact

| Period | Lagged slope *b* | HAC *t* | n |
|--------|------------------|---------|---|
| 2018-2020 | +0.0984 | **+3.05** | 34 |
| 2021-2022 | +0.0308 | +0.75 | 22 |
| 2023-2026 | +0.0002 | **+0.01** | 39 |

The lagged predictive power was real in 2018-2020 (t = +3.05) and has **fully
decayed to zero** (t = +0.01) over 2023-2026.  As the stablecoin sector matured
(and the dry-powder thesis became common knowledge), any forward edge
disappeared -- consistent with post-publication / adaptive-markets decay.

## Tradability -- turnover and cost drag

| One-way cost | Net timed return | Net HAC *t* |
|--------------|------------------|-------------|
| 10 bps | +49.4%/yr | +2.09 |
| 25 bps | +49.3%/yr | +2.08 |
| 50 bps | +49.0%/yr | +2.07 |

Average monthly switch rate is only **8.9%** (supply growth is positive in most
months, so the signal rarely flips), so costs are *not* the binding constraint
here.  The binding constraint is that the net timed series is **not
distinguishable from buy-and-hold BTC** (excess t = +0.72) once you account for
the fact that it is simply long BTC most of the time during a bull market.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds the effect when it is planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) the lagged
predictive regression recovers a planted dry-powder premium and reads ~zero on
the null:

| Planted premium | Lagged slope *b* | HAC *t* |
|-----------------|------------------|---------|
| 0.00 (null) | -0.0014 | -0.13 |
| +0.04 | +0.0386 | **+3.48** |

The engine works; the real BTC tape simply does not carry a robust *lagged*
(tradable) dry-powder signal.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The tradable, one-month-lagged predictive slope is HAC
  *t* = +1.59 -- below the *t* >= 2 bar.  The contemporaneous relationship is
  significant (t = +2.15) but that is **reflexive co-movement, not forecasting**.
  There is literature and on-chain-analytics support for the dry-powder thesis,
  and the synthetic positive control confirms the engine can detect such an
  effect when it exists -- but it is not robustly present on the real lagged
  tape, and what little there was has fully decayed (t = +3.05 in 2018-2020 to
  t = +0.01 in 2023-2026).  The curated supply series is a public aggregate
  (an approximation), which can only weaken, not strengthen, this read.
  Verdict: **WEAK**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The timed strategy beats buy-and-hold on paper,
  but the **excess over buy-and-hold is insignificant (t = +0.72, bootstrap CI
  straddles zero)** -- it is beta timing in a single bull market, not alpha.
  The signal's only statistically real component is *contemporaneous*
  (non-tradable) co-movement, and its tradable component has decayed to nothing.
  Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Survivorship / data caveat -- named.** BTC spot is a single survivor asset
  (no delisting), and the supply series is a rounded public aggregate; both are
  noted on the Signal axis. No look-ahead: the signal is strictly lagged.
